title: Finite space morphisms are limits of finite finitely presented morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A space is quasi-compact if every open cover of its point space has a finite subcover, and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback to every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source, and quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. An affine morphism is representable by schemes and has affine source after every affine scheme test. Local finite presentation and local finite type are tested on compatible etale scheme charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]; finite presentation means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. A finite morphism is representable by schemes and finite on every scheme test [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be finite and assume $Y$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. There exist a small nonempty directed set $A$, spaces $X_a$ with compatible $Y$-maps, and compatible maps $p_a:X\to X_a$, such that each $X_a\to Y$ is finite and of finite presentation, every transition $X_b\to X_a$ for $b\geq a$ is a closed immersion (representable and closed on scheme tests [def-weil-closed-immersion]), hence affine, and $X\cong\varprojlim_a X_a$ as a space over $Y$. In particular $f=(X_a\to Y)\circ p_a$ for every $a$.

source.place: Tag 07VR (lemma-finite-in-finite-and-finite-presentation); transitions are closed immersions and hence affine on scheme tests.

proof.text: On each scheme test a finite morphism is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], so $f$ is affine. The relative-Spec correspondence gives the quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal O_X$, an identification $X\simeq\operatorname{Spec}_Y\mathcal A$ over $Y$, and the finiteness of $\mathcal A$ on every affine etale chart. Apply [lem-sfb-space-finite-algebra-surjective-fp-colimit] with the given qcqs base $Y$ to obtain a small nonempty directed set $I$ and a colimit cocone $\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A$ with finite finitely presented algebras and surjective transitions.

Set $X_i=\operatorname{Spec}_Y\mathcal A_i$. Contravariance of the relative-Spec correspondence sends $\alpha_{ji}$ to $t_{ji}:X_j\to X_i$ and $\alpha_i$ to $p_i:X\to X_i$. Functoriality supplies the identity, composition and cone equations, including $f=(X_i\to Y)\circ p_i$. Its property tests give that each $X_i\to Y$ is finite and of finite presentation: the finite presentations are algebra presentations, so no module finite-presentation assumption is made.

Choose a jointly surjective family of affine etale scheme charts $U_\lambda=\operatorname{Spec}R_\lambda\to Y$ by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. For fixed $j\ge i$, put $V_{i\lambda}=X_i\times_YU_\lambda$. By the relative-Spec chart formula these are affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal A_i(U_\lambda))$; they form an etale covering of $X_i$ by the fibre-product covering lemma. The pullback of $t_{ji}$ to $V_{i\lambda}$ is $V_{j\lambda}\to V_{i\lambda}$, induced by the surjective ring map $\alpha_{ji}(U_\lambda)$. The affine characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes this a closed immersion. Apply [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-atlas-locality] to this target covering: $t_{ji}$ is representable and closed on every scheme test. On those tests it is affine by the same affine characterization, so $t_{ji}$ is affine as well.

By [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages], the sheaf limit $L=\varprojlim_iX_i$ is an algebraic space and its projections $q_i$ are affine. Choose $i_0\in I$ and give $L$ the map $q_{i_0}$ followed by $X_{i_0}\to Y$. For any $i$, choose $j\ge i,i_0$; the cone equations show that $q_i$ has the same composite to $Y$. Hence $L$ is a limit also over $Y$: a cone from $W/Y$ gives a unique map $W\to L$, and the equation with $q_{i_0}$ makes it a $Y$-map. The map $L\to Y$ is affine by composition of affine morphisms [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality]. The algebra colimit and relative-Spec anti-equivalence show that $(X,(p_i))$ is a limit in the full subcategory of spaces affine over $Y$: for each quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal B$, compatible maps $\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal B$ factor uniquely through $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$. The cone $L$ is a limit in that subcategory too. The unique cone maps $X\to L$ and $L\to X$ are inverse, since their composites have the identity projections and uniqueness forces each to be the identity. Thus $X\simeq L$ over $Y$, with precisely the maps $p_i$, proving the asserted limit among all spaces over $Y$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_finitePresentation_limit_of_finite {S : Scheme.{u}} {X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ g ↦ IsFinite g.left) f.hom.hom) (hqc : CompactSpace (Point Y.obj.obj)) (hqs : ∀ (U V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Y.obj.obj) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y.obj.obj), IsAffine U.left → IsAffine V.left → CompactSpace (Point (Limits.pullback a b))) : ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : PartialOrder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)) (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Over Y) (π : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj (Over.mk f) ⟶ D), (∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ g ↦ IsFinite g.left) (D.obj i).hom.hom.hom ∧ MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation (D.obj i).hom ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact (D.obj i).hom.hom.hom ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal (D.obj i).hom.hom.hom)) ∧ (∀ (i j : Iᵒᵖ) (a : i ⟶ j), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ g ↦ IsClosedImmersion g.left) (D.map a).left.hom.hom ∧ IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ g ↦ IsAffineHom g.left) (D.map a).left.hom.hom) ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk (Over.mk f) π))
